description: Create NGBoostDiCE_WaterQuality_Kadiwal_Final_V2.ipynb with revised preprocessing order (Impute->Scale->Split), hyperparameter tuning (Grid Search + 5-fold CV), conditional SMOTE-ENN, updated DiCE constraints (WHO generation + Permenkes evaluation), and academic references per section.
steps: Create NGBoostDiCE_WaterQuality_Kadiwal_Final_V2.ipynb as a valid ipynb JSON file based on the structure of V1 but with the following changes throughout
Cell 0: Colab badge link updated to V2 filename

Cell 1: Markdown header updated - remove 'Zero Leakage' narrative, replace with explanation that preprocessing follows Al Bataineh et al. (2026) Algorithm 3 and Patel et al. (2022). Update alur to: Impute -> Scale -> Split 70/15/15
Cell 2: pip install cell - add dice-ml and imblearn to the single pip install (so it is: ngboost xgboost scikit-learn pandas numpy matplotlib seaborn dice-ml imbalanced-learn scipy)
Cell 3: Imports - add GridSearchCV, SMOTEENN from imblearn.combine, DecisionTreeRegressor from sklearn.tree
Cell 4: Data loading - keep Google Drive mount + local fallback + upload pattern (same as V1)
Cell 5: EDA cell - add markdown reference: 'Langkah ini mengikuti standar eksplorasi data sebelum preprocessing.' Keep same visualizations as V1

Cell 6: PREPROCESSING - NEW ORDER: Step 1: Median imputation on ENTIRE X dataset. Step 2: MinMaxScaler on ENTIRE imputed X. Step 3: Split scaled data 70/15/15 stratified. Add reference to Al Bataineh et al. (2026) 'Step 1: 1.1 Handle missing values using median imputation, 1.2 Normalize all features to range [0,1], 1.3 Split D' and Patel et al. (2022)

Cell 7: SMOTE-ENN CONDITIONAL - Apply SMOTE-ENN on training data only. Train NGBoost with and without SMOTE-ENN. Compare F1 scores. If SMOTE-ENN does NOT improve, use original data and document finding. Reference: Zhu et al. (2023)

Cell 8: HYPERPARAMETER TUNING (Grid Search + 5-fold CV) - For NGBoost: grid over n_estimators [100,200,300,500], learning_rate [0.01,0.02,0.05,0.1], minibatch_frac [0.5,0.8,1.0], base learner max_depth [3,4,5,8]. For XGBoost: n_estimators [100,200,300,500], max_depth [3,4,5,6,8], learning_rate [0.01,0.05,0.1], subsample [0.7,0.8,0.9]. For Random Forest: n_estimators [100,200,300,500], max_depth [None,10,15,20], min_samples_split [2,5,10]. Reference: Nnadi et al. (2026), Zhu et al. (2023), Duan et al. (2020). NOTE: For NGBoost grid search, implement manually with loops since NGBClassifier may not work with sklearn GridSearchCV directly.

Cell 9: TRAINING with best hyperparameters - NGBoost (Bernoulli, Natural Gradient/Fisher Info, DecisionTreeRegressor(max_depth=best), n_estimators=best, lr=best, minibatch_frac=best, col_sample=0.8, Early stopping on validation set). XGBoost with best params. RF with best params. Reference: Duan et al. (2020) for NGBoost defaults
Cell 10: EVALUASI - same metrics as V1 (Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1, AUC-ROC, NLL, ECE) but on the new preprocessing pipeline
Cell 11: McNemar's test - keep from V1
Cell 12: Uncertainty Zone Analysis - keep from V1
Cell 13: Calibration Curves - keep from V1
Cell 14: ROC Curves - keep from V1
Cell 15: KDE Distributions - keep from V1
Cell 16: Confusion Matrices - keep from V1
Cell 17: Feature Importance - keep from V1
Cell 18: 5-Fold Cross-Validation - UPDATE to use the new preprocessing order (impute+scale on full data, then CV splits). Reference paper
Cell 19: RINGKASAN HASIL - update narrative to match new methodology
Cell 20: Markdown - DiCE section header with references to Mothilal et al. (2020)

Cell 21: DiCE setup - NGBoostWrapper class (simpler since data is already scaled before split). WHO constraints for GENERATION: pH 6.5-8.5, Hardness 0-500, Solids/TDS 0-1000, Chloramines 0-3, Sulfate 0-500, Conductivity 181-753 (data-driven P5-P95), Organic_carbon 2.2-28.3 (data-driven P5-P95), Trihalomethanes 0-200, Turbidity 0-4
Cell 22: DiCE data preparation and explainer creation
Cell 23: Sample selection (8 samples - 4 Not Potable various confidence, 4 Potable various confidence)
Cell 24: Generate counterfactuals - Not Potable -> Potable direction

Cell 25: EVALUASI CONSTRAINT - Two-tier: WHO for generation feasibility, Permenkes No.2/2023 for regulatory compliance evaluation (pH 6.5-8.5, TDS<300, Turbidity<3, Chloramines 0.2-0.5). Features not in Permenkes use WHO.
Cell 26: Rekomendasi Preskriptif output (same format as V1 but with constraint compliance info)
Cell 27: Evaluasi Counterfactual metrics: Validity, Proximity, Sparsity, Diversity, Feasibility. Reference: Mothilal et al. (2020)
Cell 28: Perbandingan Canada vs Kadiwal (keep from V1 cell 17 but update methodology description)
Every markdown cell before a major section must include academic reference in format: 'Langkah ini mengikuti [Author et al. (Year)] yang...'
acceptance_criteria: All code cells parse as valid Python (ast.parse)
Preprocessing order is: impute full data -> scale full data -> split (NOT split first)
Grid Search + 5-fold CV hyperparameter tuning cell exists for all 3 models with specified parameter grids
SMOTE-ENN conditional comparison exists (train with and without, pick better or document finding)
DiCE permitted_range uses WHO constraints for generation
Permenkes No.2/2023 evaluation cell exists for counterfactual compliance
No mention of 'Zero Leakage' in the notebook - replaced with Al Bataineh et al. (2026) reference
Academic references present in markdown cells before each major section
Notebook retains: McNemar test, Uncertainty Zone, Calibration, ROC, KDE, Confusion Matrices, Feature Importance, 5-fold CV, Canada vs Kadiwal comparison
verification: python3 -c "import json; nb=json.load(open('NGBoostDiCE_WaterQuality_Kadiwal_Final_V2.ipynb')); print(f'Cells: {len(nb[\"cells\"])}'); assert len(nb['cells']) >= 25, 'Too few cells'"

python3 -c "import json, ast; nb=json.load(open('NGBoostDiCE_WaterQuality_Kadiwal_Final_V2.ipynb')); errors=[i for i,c in enumerate(nb['cells']) if c['cell_type']=='code' and not (lambda s: (ast.parse(s), True)[-1] if s.strip() else True)(''.join(c['source']).replace('!pip','#pip').replace('!apt','#apt'))]; print(f'Parse errors in cells: {errors}'); assert not errors"

python3 -c "import json; nb=json.load(open('NGBoostDiCE_WaterQuality_Kadiwal_Final_V2.ipynb')); src=''.join(c for cell in nb['cells'] for c in cell['source']); assert 'Zero Leakage' not in src or 'zero leakage' not in src.lower(), 'Zero Leakage still present'; assert 'Al Bataineh' in src, 'Missing Al Bataineh reference'; assert 'SMOTE' in src, 'Missing SMOTE'; assert 'GridSearch' in src or 'grid_search' in src or 'param_grid' in src, 'Missing grid search'; print('Content checks passed')"
